title: Two forms of the Latin rite
word: Two forms of the Latin rite
hook: the Mass of 1970 and the older Latin Mass both have devoted followers, with strong feelings

segments.voice: Yesterday, many customs: Monica in Milan, and Ambrose telling her to follow the church she was in. Your line was many customs. Did you ask about a custom before correcting it? Day one thousand four hundred four.

Two friends meet for brunch after Sunday Mass. They went to different churches. One sat near the front at a Mass in English, the priest facing the people across the altar, the whole room singing the responses. The other went to a Latin Mass: chant, long silences, the priest facing the same way as the people, toward the altar. The first priest's opening words were in her own language. The second began at the foot of the altar with a psalm in Latin. Both friends love what they went to. Both have, at some point, said something sharp about the other's. The coffee arrives. Neither of them is leaving the Church. Today, two forms of the Latin rite.
screen: `BRUNCH AFTER TWO MASSES.` → `ENGLISH AND SINGING. LATIN AND CHANT.` → `BOTH LOVE WHAT THEY WENT TO.`

segments.voice: After the Second Vatican Council, Pope Paul VI issued a revised Roman Missal. That is the Mass in the reformed books, usually in the local language, the one the first friend went to. The older Missal, used before the reform, is the Mass in Latin that the second friend loves. The older Mass opens with prayers at the foot of the altar, built on a psalm. In the Douay-Rheims: "I will go in to the altar of God: to God who giveth joy to my youth." Some people drawn to it speak of reverence, silence, and continuity with the generations who prayed it. Some drawn to the reformed Mass speak of hearing the readings in their own tongue, a wider sweep of scripture, and joining aloud in the prayers. The popes themselves have handled this differently. Pope Benedict XVI widened permission for the older Mass and described the two as two expressions of the one Roman rite. Pope Francis later placed the older Mass under each bishop's oversight and taught that the reformed books are the one expression of the Roman rite's law of prayer. Some Catholics on each side have felt each decision deeply. Here is what both Masses share. The same sacrifice of Christ, made present. The same Gospels proclaimed. The same Lord received in communion. And one prayer prayed in both: the old Roman Canon, kept in the reformed Missal as the first Eucharistic Prayer. Paul begged a divided church in Corinth, in the Douay-Rheims, "that there be no schisms among you." Strong feelings, held by people who are in one Church.
screen: `THE REFORMED MISSAL AFTER THE COUNCIL.` · `THE OLDER MASS: TO THE ALTAR OF GOD.` · `TWO POPES, TWO DECISIONS.` · `ONE SACRIFICE, ONE ROMAN CANON.` · then, large: `THAT THERE BE NO SCHISMS AMONG YOU.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray for peace between them. Settle, and breathe. Recall one sharp sentence about how other people worship, one you've heard or said. Then bring to mind a real person on the other end of it: a friend, a parent, a priest, someone online. See them in the pew, at the moment of the Mass they care about most. If you pray, you can ask God for peace between Catholics who love different forms of the Mass, and name that one person. If you don't, simply hold them in mind with good will, and let one sharp sentence you've said, or thought, go. The bell holds the time.
Two forms of the Latin rite. The reformed Mass from after the Second Vatican Council and the older Latin Mass: both Roman, both offering the one sacrifice, both deeply loved. Today's word.
screen: `TWO FORMS OF THE LATIN RITE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: one church, both loved. Today, when you're about to say something cutting about a way of worship you don't share, swap it for a question: what do you love about it? Day one thousand four hundred four.

howItsDone: Latin Catholic parishes celebrate the Mass in the reformed Roman Missal, usually in the local language; some communities, with their bishop's permission, celebrate the older Latin Mass. Catholics may attend either, and both are celebrated as the one sacrifice of the Mass.

original.note: Latin, the law of praying is the law of believing: an old saying that ties how the Church prays to what it believes.

what a scholar hears: Summorum Pontificum (Benedict XVI) spoke of two expressions of the one Roman rite; Traditionis Custodes (Francis) named the reformed books the unique expression of its lex orandi.

notes: Sensitive topic: written to describe both forms and both papal decisions without ranking. A Keeper should check that neither side would find its position unfairly put.
The index's '1970' is not stated in the script (no source cited for the day gives it); the Missal is described as 'issued after the Second Vatican Council'. Confirm.
Douay-Rheims Psalm 42:4 ('And I will go in to the altar of God...' — leading 'And' dropped) and 1 Corinthians 1:10: confirm wording.
The prayers at the foot of the altar use Psalm 42 (Judica me) with the antiphon Introibo ad altare Dei; confirm the description 'built on a psalm'.

Summorum Pontificum: 'two expressions (usus) of the one Roman rite'; Traditionis Custodes art. 1: the books of Paul VI and John Paul II are the unique expression of the lex orandi of the Roman Rite; art. 2: the bishop regulates the older Missal in his diocese. Paraphrased; confirm, and update if Holy See policy has since changed.
Reasons people give for loving each form are attributed ('people drawn to it often speak of') and not stated as facts; confirm fair.
Roman Canon retained as Eucharistic Prayer I: confirm.
howItsDone makes no claim about how many communities celebrate the older Mass.
Title keeps the index wording 'two forms'; since Traditionis Custodes the 'ordinary/extraordinary form' language is no longer the Holy See's usage. The index may need an owner-approved retitle.

Editor: 'the same readings' corrected to 'the same Gospels' (the two lectionaries differ); 'often' and 'Catholics on each side' softened to 'some'; practice reworked so it doesn't assume which Mass the listener loves or repeat yesterday's angle; original note no longer generalizes about Catholics.
